reference_engine_version: per case — see each case's last_produced_in
provenance_note: Each case carries last_produced_on (ISO date) and last_produced_in (the workspace version at that commit), derived from git history by scripts/derive-corpus-provenance.py and re-checked in CI. They record when that case's stored values LAST CHANGED, which is what tells you whether they still describe the current solver. A single file-wide version was previously claimed here and was wrong for 37 of the 48 cases. Caveat: the version is the one under development at that commit, not necessarily a released build.

dipole-ex4-freesp-51seg.status: PH8-CHK-001: EX type 4 = current source; solves on --solver hallen with feedpoint Z=V/i0 matching the voltage-source dipole. Re-pinned 2026-08-30 (FND-118): was 74.23 + j13.9, fnec's old bespoke current-source solver, which agreed with the voltage drive to 0.02 percent rather than exactly. The current drive is now the voltage solve rescaled, so this is the voltage-drive value to the digit. The change is 0.015 ohm and the row passed its tolerance either way; it is re-pinned so the reference states what the code produces rather than what it produced. Re-pinned 2026-09-25 (FND-156): the Hallén free-end rows now extrapolate the current to the physical wire tip instead of zeroing it at the end segment's midpoint, which had shortened every wire by one segment; the dipole moves 74.24 + j13.90 -> 78.83 + j42.44 (nec2c 79.35 + j46.22).

dipole-ground-51seg.status: GN=1 PEC image-method support active; regression-gated in CI. External reference candidate captured via nec2c 1.3.1 with XQ-appended deck copy, and now CI-gated with absolute external R/X thresholds. dipole-ex4-gn2-near-ground-51seg.status: FND-118 gate, RE-PINNED. This row was frozen at 86.237810 + j12.681089 to DOCUMENT a defect: the current drive disagreed with the voltage drive by 6.5 percent over ground, and every EX4 fixture was free space so the class was ungated. The defect is now fixed and the row records the corrected answer. The two drives agree to the digit because Z = V/I is a property of the port and not of how it is driven; a current source is the voltage solve scaled by i0/I_feed, exactly, for a linear system. MY FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG and the ablation refuted it: I attributed the split to a constraint weight of 1e6 in the bespoke current-source solver, but sweeping that across nine orders of magnitude moves R by 0.28 percent against a 6.5 percent gap, and equalising the weight on both drives leaves the split intact. The real cause is that over finite ground the augmented Hallen system becomes INCONSISTENT -- the free-space homogeneous basis no longer satisfies the ground-modified operator, measured residual rising from 3e-7 to 5.8 percent -- so the port voltage is pinned only to about 4 percent and the two drives minimised slightly different objectives over a nearly flat valley. Which drive to keep was settled by an oracle that is NEITHER: the MPIE solver, a different kernel with a different ground model, answers this geometry R = 91.208. The voltage drive is 1.2 percent away; the old current drive was 5.4 percent away. Re-pinned 2026-09-25 (FND-156): the Hallén free-end rows now extrapolate the current to the physical wire tip instead of zeroing it at the end segment's midpoint, which had shortened every wire by one segment; the dipole moves 74.24 + j13.90 -> 78.83 + j42.44 (nec2c 79.35 + j46.22).

split-v-conductor-path-freesp.reference_source: fnec Hallen conductor-path solve (self-pinned regression), cross-checked against nec2c 268.56 + j452.26 on the same deck
split-v-conductor-path-freesp.status: FND-132 gate. Pins the conductor-path basis so it cannot silently regress. Probed 2026-08-30: of every deck then in corpus/, ZERO routed to this basis, because it needs a start-to-start or end-to-end REVERSED split and an ordinary end-to-start bend reduces to trivial paths. That matters beyond coverage: FND-121 was a CRITICAL finding about this exact basis being wired to only one frontend of four, and it was found by an audit rather than by the corpus, because the corpus could not reach the code. The external tolerances are wide ON PURPOSE and are not a defect being hidden: fnec's Hallen formulation differs from nec2c systematically (R within 1.4 percent here, X within 9.2 percent), which is the documented corpus-validation position for this solver. The tight gates are the self-pinned regression; the external numbers say the answer is the right shape. Re-pinned 2026-09-25 (FND-156): the Hallén free-end rows now extrapolate the current to the physical wire tip instead of zeroing it at the end segment's midpoint, which had shortened every wire by one segment; the dipole moves 74.24 + j13.90 -> 78.83 + j42.44 (nec2c 79.35 + j46.22). That fix removed a cancellation this row had been relying on: the 21-per-arm answer used to sit 1.4 percent from nec2c only because the 1/N shortening offset a real difference. Both end conditions converge to the same limit (old 295.26 + j495.96, new 304.40 + j522.25 at 81 segments per arm), while nec2c converges to about 279 + j459, so the ~11 percent R / ~13 percent X gap is a converged Hallen-vs-nec2c difference on this off-centre, near-antiresonant feed, not discretisation. The external gate is now relative (12 / 15 percent) and states that band; FND-158 tracks the difference itself.
